samples.evidence: The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:102-105) has exactly one acceptance criterion: "Type text, select it, reset the text color → the text is uncolored (default ink), not the selection color." Its Plan (lines 21-101) covers the toolbar reset, the renderer `resolveStoredColor` guard, and the *color* normalizer at the DOCX/PPTX color sinks. The diff additionally rewrites `PRST_BY_KIND` (~90 shape kinds), `DASH_VAL`, `TYPE_TO_TAG`/`DIR_TO_ATTR`/`EFFECT_TO_PRESET`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE`/`toXmlInt` in animation.ts, `ROUTING_PRST`/`KIND_TO_OOXML`/`SIZE_TO_OOXML` in connector.ts, `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE` in layout.ts, `ALGN`/`UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U`/`listLevelAttr` in text.ts, and `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`toHeadingStyleId` in docx-style-map.ts — none of which touch color. samples.summary: A function named `assertValid…` mutates the caller's request body (`normalizeSlideInlines` fills `inlines: []` / `style: {}`), making validation and repair one step on a 'replace' endpoint.
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` calls `normalizeSlideInlines(block, …)`, which assigns `block.inlines = []` and `inline.style = {}` on the request body, and the controller then both writes and echoes that mutated object (putContent returns `body as SlidesDocument`). An `asserts body is X` signature advertises a pure predicate; silently rewriting persisted deck content is a separate concern that belongs in an explicit `normalizeSlidesBody(body)` step (and arguably in `@wafflebase/slides`, where every other writer could reuse it). It also sits awkwardly against the issue's Non-Goal "No migration pass over existing documents" — legacy decks are rewritten on the next PUT.

samples.summary: ~250 lines of slides/docs *model-shape* knowledge (element kinds, group children, layout placeholders/staticElements, text bodies, notes) are hand-rolled in a NestJS controller rather than in `@wafflebase/slides` / `@wafflebase/docs`, repeating the duplication pattern this same change removed for the CRDT codec.
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlidesBody` / `assertValidLayout` / `assertValidElementData` / `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` encode the slides element model inside the backend, while the backend already depends on `@wafflebase/slides` (packages/backend/package.json:42, src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:21) where those types are defined. The branch's own lesson (docs/tasks/.../lessons.md:88-96) is that shape knowledge duplicated per writer cannot be kept in sync, which is why `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` moved into `@wafflebase/docs/model/crdt-attrs.ts`; the validator keeps the model knowledge in one consumer, so the CLI and editor cannot reuse it and it drifts when the slides model changes.

samples.summary: The same `Block` type is held to two different contracts by two arms of one endpoint (docs arm: `id`/`style`/`inlines` required, alignment allowlist; slides arm: all optional, alignment any string, inlines auto-repaired), so PUT semantics for identical content depend on the document type.
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` (docs arm) rejects a block without `id` or `inlines` and rejects an alignment outside BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS; `assertValidSlideBlocks` accepts both and passes `alignmentRule: 'string'`. rest-api.md documents the asymmetry and its round-trip rationale, but the underlying cause is that slide text bodies are stored verbatim while docs blocks go through a codec — a persistence-layer gap the API is papering over rather than a property of `Block`.

samples.summary: Two behavioral CRDT changes ship undocumented: 'a table block never gets a synthetic empty inline' in `setBlockType`, and the node-scoped attribute removal at the *block* level (docs-tables.md documents only the cell case).
samples.evidence: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469 adds `type !== 'table'` to the ensure-one-empty-inline branch (and the mirrored in-memory branch at 1494), a Tree-shape invariant with no entry in docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md, docs-collaboration.md or docs-intent-preserving-edits.md; docs-tables.md:176-187 explains node-scoped removal only for `applyCellStyle`/`applyCellSpan`, not for the `setBlockType` stale-attribute removal that now also uses `removeNodeStyle`.

samples.summary: Alias-only indirections add a layer without behavior: `toDocxHexColor` is a one-line passthrough of `toRgbHexColor`, and both stores alias the shared codec (`const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs`).
samples.evidence: docx-style-map.ts:47 `export function toDocxHexColor(color) { return toRgbHexColor(color); }`; packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts both introduce `const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs; const parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs;`. Importing the shared names directly at the call sites would remove three indirections and the risk of the local name drifting from the shared contract.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual claims check out in the working tree. The originating task doc has exactly one acceptance criterion (todo.md:102-105) and a Plan (lines 21-101) scoped to the toolbar reset, the renderer `resolveStoredColor` guard, and the *color* normalizers at the DOCX/PPTX color sinks; its Non-goals (107-112) are palette/picker UI and migration. The non-color OOXML hardening the reviewer names is all present as described: shape.ts:24 `PRST_BY_KIND` Map (~90 kinds) + :132 `DASH_VAL` used at :97/:153; animation.ts:60/:82/:100/:141/:152/:180 (`TYPE_TO_TAG`, `toXmlInt`, `DIR_TO_ATTR`, `CATEGORY_TO_CLASS`, `EFFECT_TO_PRESET`, `START_TO_NODE_TYPE`) used at :118-123 and :208-258; connector.ts:15/:45/:64; layout.ts:31; text.ts:82/:253; docx-style-map.ts:118/:139/:166 (`w:jc`, `w:pStyle`). None of these concern color, so `not-present` does not apply. `out-of-scope` does not apply either: "unrequested scope creep" and "over-/under-engineered vs the issue" are explicitly inside the design-fit lane. The one mitigating datum — the paired lessons doc (20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:45-73) records that the `<w:jc>` sibling attribute and the "an object-literal lookup is not closed, use a Map" rule arose from review rounds on this same change — only rebuts the DOCX arm and does not cover the PPTX shape/animation/connector/layout breadth, and CONTRIBUTING.md has no provision sanctioning bundled unrelated hardening. That is a partial rebuttal, not a named refutation ground, so the finding stays.

searchedFor: git diff hunks for docs/design/* in this delta
finding.summary: The canonical REST-API design doc now contradicts the code this delta adds. `rest-api.md` §"PUT validation contract" states that on the slides walk "the structural block checks (`id`, `inlines`, a present `style`) are not applied" — deliberately relaxed so a GET→edit→PUT round-trip of an older deck cannot 400. This delta adds `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:704/741), which does hold a *present* `inlines` on a slide block to a contract (array of objects, string `text`, object `style`), i.e. a structural check on `inlines` in the slides arm. The doc was not updated in the same change (the sibling DOCX doc *was* updated for `toHeadingStyleId`), leaving the documented contract wrong and the new relaxation boundary (present-only vs required) unrecorded. It also silently narrows the stated round-trip guarantee: a legacy deck whose stored inline lacks `text` now 400s on re-PUT, which the doc explicitly says must not happen.

verdict.reason: The canonical design doc already documents exactly the contract the finding says is missing/contradicted. docs/design/rest-api.md:255-256 lists the relaxed slides-arm checks as "(`id`, a present `style`)" — it does NOT say `inlines` is relaxed, so the finding's quoted doc text ("`id`, `inlines`, a present `style`") does not exist in the tree. A dedicated bullet at rest-api.md:265-279 states "`inlines` is the exception to that relaxation", explains the shared-layout-engine rationale (resolveBlockInlines/measureSegments/resolveColorAtPosition, PDF/PPTX font sweep), describes the absent-value repair (missing `inlines` -> `[]`, missing inline `style` -> `{}`, repaired body echoed), and records the present-only vs required boundary verbatim: "A value that is *present but wrong* is still a 400: `inlines` must be an array, each entry an object with a string `text`, and a present `style` must be an object." That matches the code exactly: the helper is `normalizeSlideInlines` (controller.ts:752, called at :706), which fills absent values and throws only for non-array `inlines`, non-object entries, non-string `text`, and a present non-object `style` (:756-787). The reviewer's grep for `assertValidSlideInlines`/`assertValid` missed it because the function is named `normalizeSlideInlines`, and their read window 225-274 stopped before line 279 where the present-but-wrong rule (including the `text` narrowing they call unrecorded) is stated.

finding.summary: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts` now routes every `<a:clrScheme>` slot value through `toRgbHexColor` with a `000000` fallback (a behavior change: a stored theme color the normalizer cannot express now exports as black instead of being passed through). `slides-pptx-export.md` §3 maintains an explicit taxonomy of color sinks — "omittable sinks drop the color" vs "mandatory sinks fall back to 000000" — and §5 still describes the theme as a plain `ColorScheme → <a:clrScheme>` mapping. The new mandatory sink and its fallback are not recorded there, even though the parallel DOCX change in this same delta did add a converter/failure-behavior row to `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md`. The closed-`Map` attribute lookups added here (routing `prst`, arrowhead kind/size, `prstDash`, layout `type`) are likewise undocumented in that doc's round-trip tables.

verdict.reason: The doc does record exactly what the finding says is missing. docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md:167-172 (§3) extends the omittable-vs-mandatory color-sink taxonomy with a new bullet: "The 12 `<a:clrScheme>` slots (`theme.ts`) are mandatory sinks too ... so `Theme.colors[role]` goes through the same `toRgbHexColor` and a value it cannot express exports as black rather than being passed through. See §5." And §5 is no longer a plain ColorScheme→clrScheme mapping: lines 204-208 state each slot value is a "mandatory color sink (§3)", that the value is untrusted persisted JSON from the content PUT API, that it is normalized through the shared `toRgbHexColor` returning only `[0-9A-F]{6}`, and that it "degrades to `000000` when it cannot be expressed — the slot cannot simply be omitted." This matches packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:76-78 and :94-99 precisely. The finding's quoted evidence ("grep clrScheme came up empty", "§5 still describes the theme as a plain mapping") is factually wrong against this working tree. The residual sub-claim about closed-`Map` attribute lookups is also partly covered (§5:213-226 documents the closed-Map-with-fallback pattern for animation/transition enums; §5:209-212 documents layout `type`/`matchingName`; §4:189 documents kind→prstGeom prst as the importer's inverse); what is left — per-row notes for DASH_VAL/arrowhead maps — is a documentation-granularity preference about a defensive implementation detail with no architecture or data-model change, i.e. minor at most, not a missing or parallel design doc.

finding.summary: The delta's stated design principle — "attribute lookups over persisted JSON must be closed `Map`s with an explicit fallback, because an object literal consults the prototype chain and an unknown key emits `undefined`" — is applied to connector routing/arrowheads, shape dash and layout type, but sibling sinks in the same exporter are left as bare object literals with no fallback at all: `animation.ts` `TYPE_TO_TAG[t.type]` (line 90), `DIR_TO_ATTR[t.direction]` (line 95), `CATEGORY_TO_CLASS`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE`/`EFFECT_TO_PRESET`, and `color.ts` `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` (color.ts:49) — whose own comment at color.ts:31 already asserts it is "a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value" and whose doc comment claims an "unknown-`role` arm" fallback that does not exist in code. Applying the hardening pattern to a subset leaves the exporter inconsistent and the invariant the comments claim untrue.

verdict.reason: The finding's primary location and five of its six evidence items do not exist as described. In packages/slides/src/export/pptx/animation.ts every table the finding calls a "bare object literal with no fallback" is already a closed Map with an explicit fallback: TYPE_TO_TAG = new Map (animation.ts:60) read as `TYPE_TO_TAG.get(t.type) ?? 'cut'` (animation.ts:118); DIR_TO_ATTR = new Map (animation.ts:100) read via `.get()` and gated by `dir ? ... : ''` (animation.ts:123-125); CATEGORY_TO_CLASS (animation.ts:141), EFFECT_TO_PRESET (animation.ts:152) and START_TO_NODE_TYPE (animation.ts:180) are Maps read as `START_TO_NODE_TYPE.get(anim.start) ?? 'clickEffect'` (animation.ts:208) and `preset?.cls ?? CATEGORY_TO_CLASS.get(anim.category) ?? 'entr'` (animation.ts:221-223). The cited lines are also wrong: animation.ts:90 is the msToSpd 'med' branch and animation.ts:95 is a doc comment. The only literally accurate sub-item is ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role] in color.ts (color.ts:4-17, color.ts:49), but its parameter type ThemeColor carries the closed ColorRole union, and the one path where an open persisted `role: string` can reach it is already validated by `Object.keys(ROLE_TO_SCHEME).includes(c.role)` with a black fallback (text.ts:200-219) — which is precisely the "unknown-role fallback" the color.ts:57-58 comment points at, so the comment's invariant is upheld rather than untrue. What remains is a stylistic consistency preference (object literal vs Map for one already-guarded lookup), which under the design-fit rubric is minor/taste, not a missed acceptance criterion, duplicated module, Non-Goal breach, or design-doc gap.
